We need to generate new test cases for untested input combinations, avoiding duplication. Existing groups cover normal scenarios (positive, negative, zero), edge NaN, null/illegal state. Need other cases: maybe zero entry price (division by zero) leading to Infinity or exception? Also entry and exit same but zero price? Also cost model? Actually getGrossReturn(entryPrice, exitPrice) likely does (exitPrice - entryPrice) / entryPrice. If entryPrice zero, division by zero leads to NaN or exception depending on Num implementation (maybe NaN). Should test that. Also test when entryPrice or exitPrice is negative? Could be negative price unrealistic but test. Also test when both are NaN? Already have each NaN individually. Test when both are infinite? Not needed. Also test when barSeries has multiple bars but entry/exit indices produce same price? Already zero case. Also test when entry trade is BUY vs SELL? Gross return calculation might differ based on trade type? Actually getGrossReturn(entryPrice, exitPrice) likely uses entry and exit trade types? Not given. But we can test scenario where entry trade is SELL (short) and exit BUY, expecting return formula maybe (entry - exit)/entry? Not sure. But we can add scenario with short position. Need to assume method uses entryPrice and exitPrice directly regardless of type. However we could test that for a short position, the gross return is (entryPrice - exitPrice)/entryPrice (i.e., profit when price falls). But method signature only takes entryPrice and exitPrice, no type. So maybe they compute (exit - entry)/entry irrespective of type. So short would be negative return. Already covered negative case. Might test with entryPrice zero and exitPrice zero -> NaN? Also test with entryPrice negative (invalid) maybe returns something.

Also test with BarSeries that returns Num objects with custom behavior (e.g., custom Num implementation) but that's deep.

Focus on boundary: entryPrice = 0, exitPrice >0 -> expected NaN or Infinity. Need to check typical behavior: In ta4j, Num is a wrapper (e.g., DecimalNum). Division by zero yields NaN? I think DecimalNum division by zero throws ArithmeticException? Actually DecimalNum uses BigDecimal, division by zero throws ArithmeticException. But they may use divide with MathContext and catch? Not sure. Safer to expect ArithmeticException or NaN. We can state expected ArithmeticException.

Also test when entryPrice is very small (close to zero) leading to huge return.

Also test when barSeries has null price for entry or exit (price per asset returns null) leading to NPE.

Also test when barSeries is a mock that throws exception when getPrice called.

Thus create new groups: "Gross Return – Division by Zero and Extreme Values", "Gross Return – Null Price Handling", "Gross Return – Large Return Magnitude". Provide cases.

Make sure not duplicate existing.
